meta.scene_summary: We're currently trading our privacy for AI-generated hallucinations and calling it an upgrade.

cooking.headline: Six new curl CVEs just dropped while the AI giants are quiet
cooking.summary: While OpenAI and Anthropic are busy boasting about their security, the humble tool that actually keeps the internet running just found six new holes in its floorboards. It turns out even the most battle-tested code is just waiting for a rainy day to show its cracks.
cooking.plain_english: Six security vulnerabilities were discovered in the curl data transfer tool, despite recent claims of superior security from major AI companies.

cooking.headline: Anthropic drops two more models because your current stack is already legacy
cooking.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable and Mythos 5.1, effectively ensuring that the model you spent all weekend integrating is now officially 'vintage.' It's the software equivalent of buying a new phone only for the manufacturer to announce the next version while you're still waiting for your screen protector to arrive. More details in the original article.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has released two new versions of its artificial intelligence model.

cooking.headline: Google adds 'Cyber' to their model name, as if the internet wasn't already stressful enough
cooking.summary: Google just launched Gemini 3.8 Flash and a 'Cyber' variant, because apparently, we needed to distinguish between casual AI tasks and ones that sound like they belong in a 90s hacker movie. It's a bold move to market a model like a gaming peripheral, but I suppose we all need a little more 'Cyber' in our lives before the next status update.
cooking.plain_english: Google has released two new versions of its Gemini artificial intelligence model, including one specifically labeled for security-related tasks.

cooked.headline: Amazon allegedly rigged its own ad auctions to pad the margin
cooked.summary: Amazon is being accused of rigging its ad auctions to ensure they always came out on top, which is like playing a game of poker while owning the deck. It turns out the house doesn't just win; it apparently changes the rules of the game mid-hand to make sure it wins by $20 billion.
cooked.plain_english: The Federal Trade Commission claims Amazon manipulated its advertising auction system to increase its own profits by $20 billion.

cooked.headline: Uber is laying off 10% of staff to make the company 'simpler'
cooked.summary: Uber is cutting 10% of its workforce in a quest to become 'simpler and faster,' which is corporate speak for 'we want the same output with fewer people.' It's the classic tech company strategy of trying to optimize the organization by deleting the humans instead of the technical debt. More details in the original article.
cooked.plain_english: Uber is reducing its total workforce by 10% as part of an organizational restructuring effort.

cooked.headline: Apple is doing a forensic audit of an ex-employee's laptop to find OpenAI's secrets
cooked.summary: Apple is treating a former employee's MacBook like a crime scene to prove OpenAI scraped their proprietary data. It turns out the biggest risk to your intellectual property isn't a sophisticated cyberattack, but just someone taking their work laptop home.
cooked.plain_english: Apple is using forensic analysis of a former employee's computer as evidence in a legal dispute regarding data usage by OpenAI.

cooked.headline: Someone is selling 153 million driver's licenses like they're trading cards
cooked.summary: The FBI is investigating a service that put 153 million driver's licenses up for sale, effectively turning the entire DMV database into a public API. It's the ultimate reminder that your personal data is essentially just a shared file in a very poorly secured group project.
cooked.plain_english: The FBI is investigating a website that is selling the personal information of over 153 million people, including driver's license details.

cooked.headline: Mistral turns your prompts into their homework by default
cooked.summary: Mistral decided that your private prompts are now their training data unless you're paying them enough to care. It's essentially the tech equivalent of a teacher photocopying your essay to sell as a textbook.
cooked.plain_english: Mistral automatically uses data submitted by users to train its models, unless the user has an enterprise subscription.

cooked.headline: Perplexity is citing an AI-generated echo chamber, and the feedback loop is getting weird
cooked.summary: Three websites have churned out over 200,000 'best software' pages specifically to be scraped by AI models. It turns out the 'definitive research' you're getting is just an AI reading a list written by another AI for the sole purpose of being read by an AI.
cooked.plain_english: Three websites created over 200,000 web pages containing software recommendations designed to be read by artificial intelligence, which Perplexity then uses as sources.

cooked.headline: Perplexity's citations are hallucinating their own homework
cooked.summary: A third of Perplexity's citations don't actually contain the data they claim to be referencing. It's like turning in a group project where you cited a book that doesn't exist just to pad the bibliography.
cooked.plain_english: A study found that one-third of the sources cited by Perplexity do not contain the specific information or numbers the tool claims they support.
